title: feat(agent-server): add docker runtime mode for per-conversation containers
body:
HUMAN: @neubig has tried this as part of his bigger software factory stack and it seems to be working. --- AGENT: ## Why A self-hosted Agent Server currently runs every conversation in its own process but in the server's host environment. This prevents Canvas and Automation from giving each conversation a bounded Docker environment while retaining the existing conversation API. This PR adds Docker as an optional conversation runtime. Profile selection and profile-scoped secret policy remain in their existing launch path; this runtime consumes the already resolved agent and secret references. Trusted automation setup commands continue to use the Agent Server's existing workspace APIs, while conversation-scoped traffic is forwarded to the isolated container. ## Summary - Select the configured runtime through a shared `ConversationRegistry`; application assembly contains no Docker-specific routing or lifecycle code. - Add `conversation_runtime=local|docker` plus image, memory, CPU, and PID settings. - Provision one Docker Agent Server per conversation with a distinct API/encryption key, loopback-only port, dropped capabilities, `no-new-privileges`, host UID/GID, and configured resource limits. - Mount only the selected workspace and per-conversation state into the container. - Forward existing conversation, workspace, file, and WebSocket routes to the container; keep the public API independent of the selected runtime. - Persist runtime identity and expose small lifecycle operations for status, reprovisioning, credential refresh, and release. - Synchronize the inner conversation catalog so Canvas can list and reopen Docker-backed conversations. This deliberately does not add profile policy, a credential broker, permission maps, a second host-workspace namespace, TypeScript changes, or changes to the OpenAPI weak-schema allowlist. ## Issue Number Closes #5016; incorporates the Docker work tracked by #5004 and #5007. ## How to Test The focused validation on commit `414048605` passes: ```bash uv run pytest -q \ tests/agent_server/docker_runtime \ tests/agent_server/test_server_details_router.py \ tests/agent_server/test_conversation_service.py \ tests/agent_server/test_init_router.py \ tests/agent_server/test_api.py # 205 passed uv run pre-commit run --files # all hooks passed, including Ruff and Pyright make test-server-schema # OpenAPI valid; 99 existing weak-schema locations, with no allowlist increase ``` An exact-head source image for `414048605` completed a live two-turn run with DeepSeek V4 Flash. The outer server created a bounded Docker runtime, delivered a saved secret after conversation creation, and the agent consumed it without exposing its value. The runtime was then released and reprovisioned; the selected workspace survived, the resumed turn received the secret again, and the agent finished. Deleting the conversation removed its runtime and state while leaving the outer conversation catalog healthy. Inspection confirmed a loopback-only port, host UID/GID, `HOME` on per-conversation persistence, `CapDrop=ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, 1 GiB/1 CPU/256 PID limits, and only the conversation, persistence, and selected-workspace mounts. ## Type - [x] Feature ## Notes The implementation is based directly on `main`; profile-scoped secret selection is already provided by merged #5017. Docker remains optional and the default local behavior is unchanged. ## Merge and release prerequisites None. The former direct prerequisite, #5017, is merged. ---
